member_escape_vs_weight_family.note: S is normalised, so whether the HOST or the crowd of other cluster members dominates it is set by p and by self-exclusion. p = 0 flattens the mass weighting so a 4e11 Msun host counts no more than a 1e9 Msun dwarf, and the 300-member crowd then orients S along the CLUSTER radius rather than the host's -- which is what lets the member violation collapse.  That escape is a choice inside the weight family, not a property of anisotropy.

phi_boundary_rule.note: 'inf' and 'flat' are both GLOBAL prescriptions.  They differ by 0.87 dex in the median galaxy |Phi_N|, and a potential-depth gate is a function of exactly that number, so the outer continuation of a galaxy's baryon distribution is a first-order systematic on the whole mechanism, not a detail.
